questions.explain: The chapter notes these classifiers routinely hit 85%+ accuracy because the wait signatures of these failure modes are genuinely distinct.

Because the wait signatures of memory grant pressure, allocation contention, version-store bloat, and spill pressure are genuinely distinct
Because the model can then skip the tempdb DMVs entirely
Because normalization is impossible without a classifier

questions.explain: Correlating version-store growth with the oldest open snapshot transaction identifies what is pinning cleanup — the actual mechanism.

The number of user connections
The fill factor of user indexes
Version-store growth correlated with the oldest open snapshot transaction from sys.dm_tran_active_snapshot_database_transactions

questions.explain: A static 300-second rule pages during every batch load and misses slow bleeds; a trained model learns the workload's normal rhythm and slope signatures.

It eliminates the need for sys.dm_os_performance_counters
It automatically increases max server memory
It works without any historical data

questions.explain: Killing a session with a long-running open transaction triggers a long rollback that extends the outage — the safety note must assess this first.

Because the model cannot identify session IDs
Because rollback risk must be assessed — killing a long-running transaction extends the outage via rollback
Because kills require a SQL Server restart
